Set Up a GBSG-Based AFT Data Generating Mechanism

Source: R/setup_gbsg_dgm.R
setup_gbsg_dgm.Rd

Creates a GBSG-based data generating mechanism that is fully compatible with simulate_from_dgm. It builds the mechanism with the package's internal GBSG builder and returns it as an object of class c("aft_dgm_flex", "gbsg_dgm", "list").

Usage

setup_gbsg_dgm(
  model = c("alt", "null"),
  k_treat = 1,
  k_inter = 1,
  k_z3 = 1,
  z1_quantile = 0.25,
  n_super = 5000L,
  cens_type = c("weibull", "uniform"),
  use_rand_params = FALSE,
  seed = 8316951L,
  verbose = FALSE,
  k_random_noise = 0L,
  noise_seed = 20260807L
)

Arguments

model

Character. Either "alt" for alternative hypothesis with heterogeneous treatment effects, or "null" for uniform treatment effect. Default: "alt"

k_treat

Numeric. Treatment effect multiplier applied to the treatment coefficient from the fitted AFT model. Values > 1 strengthen the treatment effect. Default: 1

k_inter

Numeric. Interaction effect multiplier for the treatment-subgroup interaction (z1 * z3). Only used when model = "alt". Higher values create more heterogeneity between HR(H) and HR(Hc). Default: 1

k_z3

Numeric. Effect multiplier for the z3 (menopausal status) coefficient. Default: 1

z1_quantile

Numeric. Quantile threshold for z1 (estrogen receptor). Observations with ER <= quantile are coded as z1 = 1. Default: 0.25

n_super

Integer. Size of super-population for empirical HR estimation. Default: 5000

cens_type

Character. Censoring distribution type: "weibull" or "uniform". Default: "weibull"

use_rand_params

Logical. If TRUE, modifies confounder coefficients using estimates from randomized subset (meno == 0). Default: FALSE

seed

Integer. Random seed for super-population generation. Default: 8316951

verbose

Logical. Print diagnostic information. Default: FALSE

k_random_noise

Integer. Number of standard-normal noise columns (noise1, noise2, ...) drawn once onto the super-population at construction. Default 0L (no noise columns; output identical to previous versions).

noise_seed

Integer. Seed for the population-level noise draw, used only when k_random_noise > 0. Default 20260807L, the committed population-noise seed (commit 2a4787bc).

Value

An object of class c("aft_dgm_flex", "gbsg_dgm", "list") with the builder's fields (df_super_rand; the true hazard ratios hr_causal, hr_H_true, hr_Hc_true, AHR, AHR_H_true, AHR_Hc_true and the list hazard_ratios; model_params, cens_params, subgroup_info, effect_modifiers, analysis_vars, model_type, n_super and seed) plus:

df_super

Super-population data frame with simulate_from_dgm()-compatible column names.

model_params$tau

Copy of model_params$sigma.

model_params$censoring

Sub-list with type, mu, tau for the censoring model.

noise_names

Character vector of noise column names (character(0) when k_random_noise = 0).

noise_scheme

"population" when noise was drawn, otherwise "none".

noise_seed

The seed used for the noise draw, or NA_integer_ when none was drawn.

Details

Internally the function calls that builder and then:

  1. Adds a df_super field with column names aligned to simulate_from_dgm() conventions (lin_pred_1, lin_pred_0, lin_pred_cens_1, lin_pred_cens_0, flag_harm).

  2. Adds a model_params$tau field (= model_params$sigma) and a model_params$censoring sub-list.

  3. Sets class to c("aft_dgm_flex", "gbsg_dgm", "list").

The original df_super_rand field is kept so that compute_dgm_cde() and print.gbsg_dgm continue to work.

Subgroup. The harm subgroup H is z1 = 1 and z3 = 1: z1 is 1 when the estrogen receptor value er is at or below its z1_quantile sample quantile in survival::gbsg (the 25th percentile by default), and z3 is 1 for premenopausal patients (meno == 0). Its indicator is flag.harm in df_super_rand and flag_harm in df_super. Under model = "null" the indicator is 0 for every patient.

Model. A Weibull accelerated failure time model is fitted with survival::survreg() to survival::gbsg, with time rfstime / 30.4375 (months), event status and treatment treat = hormon. Its covariates are treat, z1, z2, z3, z4 and z5, where z2, z4 and z5 are the quartile groups of age, pgr and nodes, entered as scores 1 to 4; under model = "alt" the interaction zh = treat * z1 * z3 is added. k_treat and k_z3 multiply the fitted treat and z3 coefficients. With AFT coefficients gamma and scale sigma, the hazard-scale coefficients are -gamma / sigma (model_params$b_hr).

Interaction (k_inter). Under model = "alt", k_inter multiplies the fitted zh coefficient, gamma[zh] <- k_inter * gamma[zh] (the default k_inter = 1 keeps the fitted value). Each patient's log hazard ratio (loghr_po = theta_1 - theta_0 in df_super_rand) is then -(gamma[treat] + gamma[zh]) / sigma in H and -gamma[treat] / sigma in its complement, so k_inter = 0 gives every patient the same hazard ratio. The exponentials of these two values are the stored AHR_H_true and AHR_Hc_true. The Cox-based hr_H_true and hr_Hc_true are fitted to stacked potential outcomes of the n_super patients drawn with replacement from the GBSG rows, and differ from them; at k_inter = 0 they still differ slightly from each other. Under model = "null", k_inter is not used.

Noise columns requested via k_random_noise are inert N(0,1) population attributes intended as candidate confounders; the builder never puts them in the outcome model. They are drawn once onto the super-population (both df_super_rand and df_super), so simulated trials and evaluation frames inherit them by row resampling.

Superseded

This function is kept so that published simulations can be reproduced. New work should use generate_aft_dgm_flex() with simulate_from_dgm(), which take any survival dataset with a 0/1 treatment column. On the GBSG data they give the same outcome model, true hazard ratios and k_inter calibration once the caller has built the GBSG covariates, at k_z3 = 1 and use_rand_params = FALSE (generate_aft_dgm_flex() has neither argument); there is no drop-in replacement call. The censoring step differs: here (with the default cens_type = "weibull") a Weibull censoring model is fitted to the resampled super-population, in which treatment is the arm assigned for simulation, not the observed treatment, and its covariate term is the fitted term multiplied by the ratio of the event-model scale to the censoring-model scale. The true hazard ratios stored in the object and the k_inter calibration are not affected; simulated censoring times are, and with them the observed times and event indicators and anything computed from them, such as the beta(Hhat) targets scored on a frame from fs_build_eval_frame(). The "Extreme Subgroup Effects" article on the package website shows the general machinery on the GBSG data, with a uniform treatment effect. This function will be deprecated in a future release.

See also

generate_aft_dgm_flex, simulate_from_dgm, compute_dgm_cde

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dgm <- setup_gbsg_dgm(model = "alt", k_inter = 2, verbose = FALSE)
dgm <- compute_dgm_cde(dgm)
print(dgm)
sim <- simulate_from_dgm(dgm, n = 400, seed = 1)
} # }
